query: For high-entropy alloys intended for thermal-insulation or radiation-resistant applications, what single intervention could reduce phonon thermal conductivity? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the physical mechanism, the predicted change relative to an otherwise comparable untreated alloy, the temperature and material-state boundaries over which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment whose result would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing lattice distortions through alloying elements with different atomic radii can reduce phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys.
generation.intervention: Alloying with elements of varying atomic radii to introduce lattice distortions
generation.mechanism: Scattering of phonons by lattice distortions, reducing phonon mean free path and thermal conductivity
generation.predicted_outcome: Decreased phonon thermal conductivity compared to untreated alloys
generation.baseline: Untreated high-entropy alloy with no lattice distortions
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 900 K to 1200 K, alloy composition: single-phase solid solution
generation.uncertainty: Effect of lattice distortions on phonon thermal conductivity at high temperatures, optimal alloy composition for maximum reduction in thermal conductivity

falsification_experiment.design: Measure phonon thermal conductivity of high-entropy alloys with varying lattice distortions at high temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If phonon thermal conductivity does not decrease with increasing lattice distortions at high temperatures, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Gap and lever. Type: tradeoff. Statement: Increasing temperature leads to higher friction coefficients and tangential forces due to lattice disorder, but simultaneously causes a sharp decrease in normal force and hardness due to thermal softening.. System: FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating. Lever: temperature. Quote: "With the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases, which leads to an increase of the tangential force and friction coefficient in the friction process."

Gap and lever. Type: future_work. Statement: The authors suggest that future work should explicitly include phonon effects to improve the accuracy of phase stability predictions.. System: CoCrFeMnNi high entropy alloy. Lever: explicit phonon effect. Quote: "especially when taking into account the error bars stated in the experiments [16] and also the fact that the explicit phonon effect is not considered in the present theory."
